_comment: One entry per waived finding. Every entry needs a `reason` — a waiver with
a blank reason fails the lint, because the only thing standing between
waive-with-reason and a rubber stamp is that the reason is written down
here, in the diff, where the next reader trips over it.
issue  the issue number the finding is on
check  "2a" | "2b" | "3"  (check 4 warns and needs no waiver)
token  the flagged token, when there is one (optional; omit to cover
every token of that check on that issue — prefer naming it)
match  a substring that must still appear in the flagged text. Rewrite
the criterion and the waiver stops matching, so the finding
returns and gets looked at again with the new words in view.
reason why the ticket is right as written
A waiver that matches nothing is reported as a note. Delete it rather than
leaving it: a file of stale waivers is how the mechanism stops meaning

waivers.reason: "Captured" names the stub provider's test fixture, not a recording obligation on the pipeline. The prompts are captured in memory by the fixture that then asserts on them; nothing is persisted, so there is no channel to name. #83's sibling criterion says the same thing as "A stub provider capturing prompts proves", which the lint does not flag — the difference is grammar, not substance. Recorded 2026-08-28 during the track-3 lint of PRDs 2-6.

waivers.match: Fake mutation tool reports a survivor
waivers.reason: "Reports" is the fake mutation tool handing a survivor to the orchestrator inside a fixture, not the pipeline recording anything. The channel that does matter — survivors delivered as normalized JSON through the project-owned adapter script — is already specified in the ticket's What-to-build, and the criterion is a test scenario, not the contract for that channel. Recorded 2026-08-28 during the track-3 lint of PRDs 2-6; an earlier edit that spliced "as normalized JSON through the adapter script" into this criterion was reverted, because rewording a scenario to satisfy a lexicon is the phrase-around-the-lint failure the tool's own docs warn about.

waivers.match: PM override behavior and recording unchanged
waivers.reason: A no-change claim about behavior that already exists, not a new obligation. Naming a channel would assert where today's code writes the PM-override record — something this slice does not change and the criterion deliberately does not pin, since pinning it wrongly would put the slice in conflict with working code. Recorded 2026-08-28 during the track-3 lint of PRDs 2-6.
